facts.statement: Thoraxion is an extinct mosasaurine mosasaur belonging to the tribe Mosasaurini that lived in the Maastrichtian of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Thoraxion () is an extinct genus of mosasaurine mosasaur in the tribe Mosasaurini, known from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age)

facts.statement: A series of small vertebrae preserved in the abdominal region of the specimen represent the gut contents of the animal.
facts.quote: A string of smaller vertebrae are preservd in abdomen region, representing the gut contents of this animal.

facts.statement: The estimated total body length of Thoraxion is about 6 metres.
facts.quote: The only known specimen of Thoraxion has an estimated total body length of 6 m.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Thoraxion within Mosasaurini, diverging after Prognathodon and Eremiasaurus but before the more derived Mosasaurus clade.
facts.quote: Thoraxion was recovered as a member of the mosasaurine tribe Mosasaurini, in a position diverging after Prognathodon and Eremiasaurus, but before a more derive clade including Mosasaurus and its closest relatives.

facts.statement: The generic name Thoraxion is derived from the Ancient Greek word for ribcage, referring to its comparatively compact ribcage.
facts.quote: The generic name, Thoraxion, is a diminutive derivative of the Ancient Greek θώραξ (thṓrax), alluding to the taxon's compact ribcage compared to that of the coeval M. lemonnieri.

facts.statement: The specific epithet tahlequahae honors Tahlequah, a southern resident orca known for complex emotional behaviours such as mourning its calves.
facts.quote: The specific name, tahlequahae, honours Tahlequah, a southern resident orca known for exhibiting complex emotional behaviours (mourning after the deaths of two of her calves).

facts.statement: More than 50 mosasaur specimens were collected from 19th‑century chalk quarries in the Mons Basin, most of which had previously been assigned to Mosasaurus lemonnieri.
facts.quote: This specimen was one of more than 50 collected during the 19th century from chalk quarries in the Mons Basin. Most of these, including IRSNB R 373, have historically been referred to Mosasaurus lemonnieri.
